ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point $O$ is the midpoint of line segment $AB$, with $OB=14\,cm$. Point $P$ divides line segment $AB$ into two parts, with $AP:PB=5:2$. Point $M$ is on line segment $AB$. If the distance from point $M$ to point $P$ is $4\,cm$, what is the length of line segment $AM$ in $cm$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: As shown in Figure 1, when point M is to the left of point P,\\
$AM=AB-(PM+BP)=28-(4+8)=\boxed{16}\,(\text{cm})$,\\
As shown in Figure 2, when point M is to the right of point P,\\
$AM=AB-BM=AB-(BP-PM)=28-(8-4)=\boxed{24}\,(\text{cm})$.\\
In summary, $AM=16\,\text{cm}$ or $24\,\text{cm}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The attached figure is a horizontal line segment with labels arranged from left to right as A, O, P, B. The point M is not shown in the diagram, so with PM = 4 cm and M on AB, M can lie on either side of P as long as it remains on the segment. Reasoning: Place A at coordinate 0 and B at coordinate AB on the same line. Since O is the midpoint of AB and OB = 14 cm, the whole segment AB = 2 × 14 = 28 cm, so B has coordinate 28. Since AP:PB = 5:2, AP = (5/7) × 28 = 20 cm, so P has coordinate 20. The condition PM = 4 cm gives |x_M - 20| = 4, so x_M = 16 or x_M = 24. Since AM is the distance from A at coordinate 0 to M, AM = 16 cm or 24 cm.
